simple_definition: A chip company that keeps some of its own factories but sends more and more of its production, especially the most advanced chips, to outside contract factories.
technical_definition: Manufacturing strategy in which an IDM reduces or stops investment in new wafer fabs (and often back-end assets), retains in-house capacity for differentiated processes (e.g. analog, power), and outsources leading-edge logic to foundries and assembly/test to OSATs.
where_used: IDM strategy statements 2005-2010 (Infineon, Amkor 10-K, IC Insights)
example: Infineon (2007) kept power logic in-house and farmed out advanced logic to foundries.

simple_definition: A simple, standard set of rules (published around 1979-80) that let people design chips without knowing every detail of the factory that would make them.
technical_definition: Structured VLSI system-design methodology and scalable layout design rules developed by Carver Mead (Caltech) and Lynn Conway (Xerox PARC), published as 'Introduction to VLSI Systems' (Addison-Wesley, 1979/1980); simplified the interface between design and fabrication and underpinned multi-project chip services (MPC79, MOSIS).
where_used: History of chip design, EDA and the fabless/foundry split

simple_definition: AMD's name for its 2008-2009 plan to stop owning chip factories by moving them into a separate company it partly owned.
technical_definition: AMD's strategy under which it contributed its Dresden fabs and manufacturing staff to GLOBALFOUNDRIES (closed 2 March 2009) in exchange for GF securities and a Wafer Supply Agreement, becoming a design-focused (fabless) company.

simple_definition: When a big electronics company turns its in-house chip division into a separate company, either by listing it or selling it.
technical_definition: Separation of a diversified group's semiconductor operations into a stand-alone entity via IPO/spin-off (Siemens to Infineon 1999, Motorola to Freescale 2004) or sale to investors (Agilent SPG 2005, Philips Semiconductors to NXP 2006).

simple_definition: When a chipmaker with its own factories also pays a contract factory to make some chips, so it can add or drop that outside work as demand rises and falls.
technical_definition: IDM practice of placing a variable share of wafer demand at foundries to absorb cyclical swings without building fab capacity; described by Morris Chang as the pre-fabless foundry market ('leftovers') and by EDN for TI's use of TSMC, UMC and SMIC.
